# MASTER DEVELOPMENT PROMPT — PUVIN.IN

## Project: PUVIN — Advanced MEAN Stack Website and WordPress-Like CMS

**Existing Website:** https://puvin.in/

**Project Type:** Personal Developer Portfolio + Business Website + Advanced Content Management System

**Technology:** MongoDB, Express.js, Angular, Node.js, TypeScript

**Objective:** Build a beautiful, modern, high-performance, scalable and production-ready website for PUVIN.IN, including a fully functional WordPress-inspired CMS, blog platform, portfolio manager, visual page builder, advanced admin dashboard, SEO management and secure backend.

---

# 1. YOUR ROLE AND PRIMARY INSTRUCTIONS

Act as an expert full-stack software architect, senior Angular developer, Node.js backend engineer, UI/UX designer, MongoDB database architect, SEO engineer, application security specialist and DevOps engineer.

You are responsible for designing and implementing the complete PUVIN.IN ecosystem.

Do not create only a landing page, static HTML template, or dashboard mockup.

I need a genuine full-stack application with working frontend components, backend services, database integration, CRUD operations, authentication, content publishing and production deployment configuration.

Follow these rules:

1. Use the MEAN Stack as the primary technology stack.
2. Use TypeScript across the frontend, backend and shared interfaces.
3. Use the latest compatible, stable, production-ready framework versions. Record the actual selected versions.
4. Use Angular standalone components and modern Angular architectural practices.
5. Design mobile-first and support all screen sizes.
6. Keep public website, admin dashboard, backend services and database models modular.
7. Avoid unnecessary dependencies and overengineering.
8. Do not fabricate personal information, testimonials, client projects, professional achievements or contact details.
9. Every content module must load its actual data from the API or clearly identified seed data.
10. All admin forms, buttons, workflows and content-management actions must function.
11. Never leave placeholder implementations or disconnected fake CRUD screens.
12. Support local development, staging and production deployment.
13. Document security, deployment, backups and maintenance.
14. Build incrementally, testing each module before proceeding.

The platform should provide the ease of content management associated with WordPress while retaining the flexibility, performance and architecture of a custom MEAN application.

It does not need to execute PHP or support WordPress plugins directly. Build equivalent native features or documented extension interfaces.

# 2. ANALYZE THE EXISTING PUVIN.IN WEBSITE

Before development, examine:

https://puvin.in/

Perform an audit of the publicly accessible website.

Identify:

- Existing homepage sections and messaging
- Existing branding, logo and typography
- About Me and professional information
- Current frontend, backend and database skills
- Services and development offerings
- Portfolio projects and case studies
- Existing blog content, if any
- Contact forms and contact information
- Header and footer structures
- Existing URLs and navigation links
- Existing metadata and SEO elements
- Mobile usability and accessibility issues
- Image assets and content that can legitimately be reused
- Theme-demo navigation, dummy content and placeholders
- Website performance and technical limitations

The homepage currently describes a full-stack developer and shows portfolio, services, development process and hire-me content.

Use that as the initial business direction.

Treat PUVIN as the primary website brand. Make the portfolio owner's display name, biography, title, professional skills, contact details and social profiles fully editable through the admin dashboard.

Preserve real verified content where appropriate.

Do not blindly copy the current theme or its potentially licensed assets.

Do not import template-demo pages, dummy projects or inaccurate contact numbers as production content.

If any page cannot be accessed, report the limitation and provide a manual import option instead of inventing its content.

Create a migration inventory and old-URL-to-new-URL mapping before launch.

# 3. TECHNOLOGY STACK

## Frontend

Use:

- Angular with standalone components
- TypeScript in strict mode
- Angular Router
- Angular Signals where appropriate
- Angular HttpClient
- Angular Reactive Forms
- Angular SSR and hydration
- Hybrid rendering with SSR, SSG and CSR
- Tailwind CSS for styling
- Angular CDK for accessible interactive components
- Lucide icons or a comparable consistent icon system
- Responsive image components
- An accessible charting library for dashboard analytics

Use Angular's recommended server rendering architecture.

Keep the frontend strongly typed, reusable, maintainable and optimized.

## Backend

Use:

- Node.js LTS
- Express.js
- TypeScript
- RESTful API architecture
- Mongoose with MongoDB
- Schema validation
- Centralized error handling
- Structured application logging
- Secure cookie-based authentication
- Server-enforced role-based access control
- API rate limiting
- Background jobs for scheduled operations
- OpenAPI / Swagger documentation

## Database

Use MongoDB with Mongoose schemas.

Prefer MongoDB Atlas for managed production hosting, with configurable support for a self-hosted MongoDB instance.

Use indexes, data validation, appropriate relationships and optimized queries.

## Additional Services

Use modular provider interfaces for:

- SMTP email
- Media storage such as S3-compatible storage or Cloudinary
- Optional Redis caching and job queues
- Optional privacy-friendly analytics
- Optional Google Analytics 4 integration
- Optional CDN
- Optional webhooks and external integrations

Avoid requiring a paid service when a suitable self-hosted option is possible.

  - backup/
- docs/

# PUVIN.IN — COMPLETE AXEVIA-INSPIRED UI/UX TRANSFORMATION PROMPT

## PROJECT TYPE: REDESIGN THE EXISTING WEBSITE

I already have a website generated in this Craft Anything project.

**Current project:** puvin.in

**Current local preview:** http://127.0.0.1:55734/

**Existing production website:** https://puvin.in/

**NEW DESIGN REFERENCE:**
https://preview.themeforest.net/item/axevia-personal-portfolio-wordpress-theme/full_screen_preview/65169316

**Direct reference demo:**
https://softivus.com/wp/axevia/

## MOST IMPORTANT INSTRUCTION

I am NOT requesting a completely new website or an unrelated redesign.

I want you to transform the UI/UX of the **EXISTING PUVIN.IN PROJECT** into a premium, cinematic, futuristic, interactive developer portfolio strongly inspired by the Axevia reference.

The visual result should reproduce the reference's overall design language, spatial composition, visual hierarchy, typography proportions, motion quality, interactive patterns and immersive user experience as closely as practical, while retaining PUVIN branding and using an original implementation.

**DO NOT:**
- Rebuild the application from scratch unnecessarily.
- Delete existing backend functionality.
- Replace Angular with WordPress or React.
- Remove MongoDB, Express.js or Node.js.
- Destroy existing CMS functionality.
- Delete existing database records.
- Replace current real content with fabricated information.
- Use a generic Bootstrap portfolio design.
- Deliver another ordinary white portfolio template.
- Use static screenshots to imitate interactive elements.
- Copy proprietary theme source code or unlicensed demo assets.

**DO:**
- Keep the existing MEAN Stack architecture.
- Completely overhaul the public-facing visual experience.
- Preserve existing backend APIs and database integration.
- Reuse working application logic.
- Build reusable Angular UI components.
- Implement meaningful interactive animations.
- Make the final result visually faithful to the Axevia design direction.
- Update CMS controls to support the new design.
- Keep everything responsive, accessible, and production-ready.

---

# PHASE 1 — ANALYZE BOTH WEBSITES

Before coding, inspect:

1. The current PUVIN.IN local project.
2. The existing homepage and its components.
3. The Axevia preview and its working interactions.
4. The frontend architecture.
5. Existing API services.
6. Existing backend modules.
7. Existing CMS and admin dashboard.
8. Global styles and theme configuration.

Open the Axevia reference in a browser and inspect its main pages, navigation, animated scenes and responsive behavior.

Inspect desktop and mobile versions.

Record the following:

- Page compositions
- Header positioning
- Navigation behavior
- Hero layout
- Font hierarchy
- Background colors
- Accent colors
- Image treatment
- Animation sequences
- WebGL effects
- Mouse interactions
- Scroll interactions
- Content density
- Section spacing
- Project transitions
- Blog layouts
- Contact layout
- Footer styling
- Mobile adaptations

Create a short design audit before starting implementation.

Compare the reference against the current local PUVIN preview.

Identify exactly which existing UI components must be replaced or restyled.

Retain working backend and business logic wherever possible.

If a reference interaction cannot be inspected, explain that limitation and create a grounded approximation from the available visual evidence rather than pretending it was verified.

---

# PHASE 2 — GLOBAL DESIGN SYSTEM

## Overall Design Identity

Transform PUVIN.IN into an immersive creative-developer portfolio.

The design direction is:

**Dark + Minimal + Futuristic + Experimental + Cinematic + Technical + Interactive.**

Use a visual language inspired by the reference:

- Near-black backgrounds
- Deep charcoal surfaces
- Large editorial typography
- High-contrast white text
- Muted gray supporting text
- Technical micro-labels
- Precise geometric grids
- Fine hairline borders
- Structured data-like information
- Large cinematic visual regions
- Subtle background textures
- Monochrome imagery
- Sophisticated hover treatments
- Fluid page transitions
- Deliberate motion design

Avoid excessive colored gradients, bulky cards, generic dashboard aesthetics or randomly placed effects.

## Color System

Use the reference design as the primary color guide.

Create editable semantic design tokens.

Suggested starting values:

--color-background: #080808

--color-surface: #101010

--color-surface-raised: #181818

--color-text-primary: #F5F5F3

--color-text-secondary: #A3A3A3

--color-border: #2A2A2A

--color-accent: configurable

--color-success: #A3E635

--color-overlay: rgba(0,0,0,0.85)

Use the actual reference styling to refine these values.

Any accent color must be used intentionally and sparingly.

## Typography

Use a combination of:

- Big Shoulders Display for expressive oversized headings, if appropriate
- Inter for body text
- Space Mono for labels, system text and technical metadata
- An appropriate editorial serif or display font when needed

Load fonts responsibly using licensed or open-source font files.

Create responsive typography using CSS clamp().

Suggested visual hierarchy:

- Hero display: 80–180px on desktop, depending on composition
- Primary headings: 56–100px
- Section headings: 36–72px
- Body text: 15–18px
- Technical labels: 10–13px

Maintain reference-like proportions rather than applying these sizes blindly.

## Layout and Spacing

Use:

- Full-viewport compositions where appropriate
- Oversized headings
- Generous negative space
- Editorial asymmetric layouts
- Technical sidebars
- Carefully positioned metadata
- Fixed or sticky navigation where appropriate
- Full-bleed media areas
- Thin dividing lines
- Balanced alignment
- Consistent responsive gutters

The result should look like a professionally art-directed interactive experience, not a generic website assembled from cards.

---

# PHASE 3 — IMMERSIVE LOADING EXPERIENCE

Implement an Axevia-inspired cinematic loading experience.

The reference includes a system-style boot screen, performance selection and an entry interaction.

Build an original PUVIN boot experience with the same general interaction style.

## Loading Screen

Use a full-screen dark loading interface.

Elements:

- PUVIN.IN branding
- Technical initialization text
- Animated loading indicator
- Actual asset-loading progress where measurable
- Performance-mode selector
- Enter button
- Subtle motion graphics
- Smooth transition into the main website

Suggested interface labels:

PUVIN SYSTEM

INITIALIZING EXPERIENCE

WEBGL ENGINE

READY TO EXPLORE

ENTER WEBSITE

## Performance Modes

Implement:

HIGH

MEDIUM

SAVER

High mode enables detailed WebGL visual effects.

Medium mode reduces rendering complexity.

Saver mode removes heavy effects and provides optimized static visual alternatives.

Remember the user's preference where appropriate.

Do not display artificial loading percentages or force unnecessary delays.

Provide an immediate Skip / Enter option.

The loading experience must never prevent access to the site if a WebGL resource fails.

## Audio

Support an optional sound module only if meaningful, licensed or original audio assets are available.

Audio must be OFF by default.

Never autoplay audible sound without user interaction.

Provide mute and unmute controls.

If audio is unavailable, omit the feature rather than displaying a fake control.

---

# PHASE 4 — HOME PAGE COMPLETE REDESIGN

The homepage is the most important part of this redesign.

Remove the current conventional white hero with the large static portrait layout.

Replace it with a dramatic Axevia-inspired immersive composition.

## 4.1 Hero Section

Create a visually striking full-screen developer introduction.

Use:

- Full-height near-black background
- Interactive 3D artwork or particle portrait
- Large uppercase typography
- Minimal technical metadata
- Subtle motion
- Clear personal identity
- Availability indicator
- Primary contact CTA
- Portfolio navigation CTA

Use existing verified profile data.

Do not hardcode demo names, experience years or project counts.

Example headline:

**I BUILD DIGITAL EXPERIENCES THAT FEEL ALIVE.**

Supporting text:

"Full-stack development, thoughtful interfaces, scalable systems and creative web experiences."

Technical metadata:

CORE_ID: PUVIN

ROLE: FULL STACK DEVELOPER

STACK: ANGULAR / NODE.JS / MONGODB

STATUS: AVAILABLE FOR PROJECTS

Use actual profile settings from the CMS for the displayed name, role, skills and availability.

Create an editorial composition that balances oversized text and the WebGL visual.

## 4.2 Three.js Particle Portrait

This is a signature feature.

Implement a real interactive particle-based visual using Three.js and WebGL.

The effect should:

- Use a licensed or owner-provided portrait image
- Form the image from thousands of points or particles
- Respond subtly to mouse movement
- Disperse around the pointer
- Reform smoothly
- Include realistic depth
- Use smooth easing
- Support high-DPI displays
- Resize responsively
- Maintain a stable frame rate
- Stop rendering when not visible
- Reduce complexity on mobile

Use an independent Angular component such as:

ParticlePortraitComponent

Use Angular lifecycle hooks and browser-only initialization.

Do not initialize WebGL during server-side rendering.

Dispose of graphics resources and event listeners correctly.

Use a static optimized image fallback when WebGL is unavailable or the user prefers reduced motion.

Do not build a decorative particle system that covers important text.

## 4.3 Alternative Homepage Visual Modes

Architect the homepage to support several configurable hero variants inspired by the reference:

1. PARTICLE PORTRAIT — Interactive image particles.
2. CRT PORTRAIT — Retro digital display, scanlines and subtle shader distortion.
3. ORBIT — Dispersing and reforming point-cloud visual.
4. TYPOGRAPHIC GLOBE — Rotating sphere composed of professional keywords.
5. EDITORIAL — Typography-heavy layout with halftone portrait.
6. LIGHT EXPERIMENTAL — Spacious light-background alternative.
7. IMMERSIVE — Cinematic composition with full-screen WebGL.

Implement the particle portrait mode as the default.

Build the component architecture to make the other variants selectable from CMS settings.

Only expose a variant in the public interface after it is implemented and tested.

If the requested scope permits, implement all seven variants; otherwise deliver the default variant completely and maintain clear extension points for the remaining variants.

A variant switcher should appear only when multiple variants are enabled.

## 4.4 Developer Information Panel

Build a reference-inspired technical information display.

Display editable facts such as:

- Professional role
- Technology stack
- Main specialization
- Project availability
- Experience, if verified
